[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 240
- Description: Fix QR extraction reliability + build callable inventory-movement guard and ledger-targeted submission verification
  
  Pull requests (GitHub evidence):
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/659
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/663
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/665
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/666
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/668
  
  Details:
  Work arising from the Oscar Nibs QR batch consolidation. Four merged PRs plus one diagnosis chain, all in TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot. No ledger writes, no money moved, nothing deployed to production.
  
  ## The problem
  
  Consolidating the Oscar Nibs batches exposed three separate failure modes that all pointed the same direction: we were verifying things by hand, in the wrong place, and reading absence of evidence as evidence.
  
  1. **QR extraction was unreliable and unverified.** Single-pass pyzbar reads on dense bag labels missed codes; single vision-model reads confabulated digits (a 6 read as an 8 in a date segment). A wrong digit produces a plausible-looking code that silently fails lookup.
  2. **Quantity-only inventory movements orphan bags.** Two movements (r6126/r6127) recorded bare quantities with no QR codes. The bags left the inventory sheet while their individual QR records remained `In Inventory`, so the two ledgers drifted apart undetected until reconciled by hand. Correcting one batch required a 19-code manager reassignment.
  3. **"Not found" was being read as "failed."** Edgar returns HTTP 200 on accept, but the sheet append runs through an async Apps Script webhook that lags minutes. A check immediately after a 200 finds nothing — and the natural response, resubmitting, creates duplicate ledger rows.
  
  ## What shipped
  
  **PR #663 — `qr_decode_escalate` + QR OCR failure SOP.** Escalation ladder: pyzbar over a crop/upscale ladder, then multi-model Gemini consensus with a configurable agreement threshold, plus OCR of the printed companion label as a cross-check. Returns confidence and `needs_human`; a single vision read is never treated as truth. The SOP documents the failure mode and the escalation path.
  
  **PR #665 — SOP rule for photo-driven movements.** Where a batch is moved on the basis of photos, the movement must cite the individual QR codes rather than a count.
  
  **PR #666 — `validate_inventory_movement`.** A callable pre-flight contract enforcing #665. The trigger is **successful QR extraction**, not attachment presence — this distinction came directly from a governor correction: attachments are sometimes just a photo of people, receipts, or signatures, and must not block work. Blocks only when codes were extracted and the movement omits some or all of them, when quantity disagrees with code count, when any code is disputed/needs_human, or when non-serialized bulk is claimed while codes are present. Passes cleanly on: no attachment, undecodable photo, people/receipt photo, genuine non-serialized bulk. 16 tests, one per case, with the photo-of-people case first so it cannot regress.
  
  **PR #668 — `ledger_targets` registry + ledger-targeted submission verification.** `verify_dao_submission_landed` existed (PR #659) but still required the caller to supply spreadsheet id, A1 range and service account on every call — a fresh opportunity to hand-roll the wrong target each time. It now accepts `ledger="main", tab="offchain transactions"` and resolves through a canonical registry holding the spreadsheet id, service account, and a data-anchored range.
  
  The substantive discovery: Main Ledger tabs carry banner rows above the real header, and the offset differs per tab — `offchain transactions` has 2 banner rows (header row 3, data row 4), `offchain asset location` has 3 (header row 4, data row 5). A naive `!A:E` scan starts at row 1 and can match **banner text**, so a needle "lands" in a row unrelated to the submission. That is a false positive — it reads as verified when nothing was verified, which is worse than a false negative. Ranges are now anchored at the first data row, and an unknown ledger/tab is a hard error listing valid targets rather than a default guess. The raw path is retained as an escape hatch so no existing call site breaks.
  
  ## Errors of mine, caught before merge
  
  - **Broke the existing signature.** First version of #668 put `needle` as the leading positional argument, failing 3 pre-existing tests. Restored the original positional order and made `ledger`/`tab` keyword-only.
  - **Wrong assertion.** Asserted the registry must supply a truthy service account; `main` legitimately declares `None` meaning the default Cypher Defense SA. Changed to assert pass-through equality.
  - **Reported a gate narrower than CI.** My local test rule (compileall / ruff / format / pytest) omits `scripts/smoke_tools.py`, which CI gates on, and the box runs Python 3.10 while `smoke.yml` runs 3.11. Earlier "all gates green" reports were accurate but incomplete. A gate-fix PR follows.
  - **Misread a red CI as a code failure.** A merge was refused with "unstable" and an unnamed check; the PAT returns 403 on the checks API, so the guard was swallowing a permissions error. The PR was mergeable on retry with no code change. An unnamed check means "cannot see", not "failed".
  
  ## Verification
  
  Each PR passed locally before push: compileall, ruff check (clean on all new/changed files), ruff format, targeted tests, and the full suite. Final full-suite run on #668: 2679 passed, 2 skipped, 4 xfailed, 3 xpassed, 0 failed. #666: 2625 passed, 0 failed including the live-LLM test.
  
  ## Open, carried forward
  
  - The #666 guard is merged and callable but **not yet wired into** `dao_client`'s `report_inventory_movement.py` — enforcement is available, not automatic.
  - A Discord collaboration note was posted to `inventory-movement-oscar-chocolate-bars` sharing the guard, the banner-row trap and the extraction-escalation findings, and requesting additional test cases from the other builder.
  - Local gate rule needs `scripts/smoke_tools.py` plus a 3.11 check added.
  
  Mission tie-back: reliable per-bag QR provenance is what makes a bag's journey from a specific Brazilian farm to a buyer auditable, which is the precondition for the 10,000-hectare rainforest regeneration model being verifiable rather than asserted.
- Contributor(s): Sophia Truesight
- TDG Issued: 400.00
- Attached Filename: N/A
- Destination Contribution File Location: N/A
--------
